prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1115; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle backed into a stationary claimant vehicle while exiting a space. Scene photos requested from insured. Claimant reports a wrist fracture and has retained counsel, who has asked that all communication be directed through their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Confirmed representation and received a letter of representation. Requested medical authorization forms and the claimant's treatment records to date. Attorney indicated a demand package will follow once treatment concludes. Reminded office that the insured's policy limits and coverage terms will be verified before any settlement discussion.

Entry 3: Obtained the parking lot security footage from the property manager. Footage is partially obstructed but shows the insured vehicle reversing and making contact with the claimant's rear quarter panel. Vehicle damage estimate received from the appraiser and reviewed. Repair cost falls within the range expected for the reported impact. Rental coverage confirmed for the claimant's vehicle during repairs.

Entry 4: Received orthopedic records from the treating physician. Diagnosis is a closed fracture of the distal radius, treated with a splint followed by a cast. Physician notes the claimant is expected to return to normal activity after a recovery period, with a follow-up scheduled to assess healing. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect the medical component. Referred the file to the bodily injury unit for further evaluation.

Entry 5: Bodily injury unit reviewed the file and noted the claimant's counsel has requested an independent medical examination be deferred until the follow-up visit. Agreed to the deferral and diarized the file for review in thirty days. Insured notified of claim status and reminded to forward any correspondence received directly from the claimant or their attorney. No liability decision has been made; investigation remains open.
